drhp.business: G M Polyplast Limited operates in a single reportable business segment, namely the manufacture of plastic sheets and granules (HIPS, ABS, PET, PP and HDPE). Management describes the business as built on quality, operational excellence and customer satisfaction, and positions it to serve emerging opportunities in key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, packaging and interior solutions. During FY2025-26 the Company also promoted and incorporated Regranix Private Limited as a wholly-owned subsidiary, which had not commenced business operations as at March 31, 2026.
drhp.end_markets: Pharmaceuticals|Packaging|Interior solutions|Exports (the Company recorded foreign exchange earnings during FY2025-26)

Looking forward, management states that 'continued emphasis on product innovation, capacity expansion and sustainable manufacturing practices' positions the Company to capture emerging opportunities in pharmaceuticals, …

risks.note: MD&A states that 'Volatility in raw material prices, closely linked to fluctuations in petrochemical feedstocks, continues to introduce uncertainty into cost structures and profitability', and repeats persistent raw-material price volatility under Risks and Concerns. Cost of materials consumed is by far the dominant cost line for a plastic sheets-and-granules converter, so feedstock swings pass straight through to margin.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility tied to petrochemical feedstocks

risks.note: MD&A flags that 'Tightening environmental regulations around plastic waste management continue to demand higher investment in sustainable materials, waste recycling infrastructure and compliance mechanisms, which may elevate operational costs', and that compliance with mandatory Extended Producer Responsibility norms across the value chain 'remains an ongoing area for improvement'.
risks.risk: Tightening plastic-waste environmental regulation and EPR compliance

risks.note: The Company notes India has implemented bans on identified single-use plastics and continues to strengthen Plastic Waste Management Rules, while 'enforcement remains inconsistent in several regions' - creating both compliance-cost risk and an uneven competitive playing field.
risks.risk: Regulatory uncertainty: single-use plastic bans, evolving Plastic Waste Management Rules and inconsistent enforcement

risks.note: 'Growing public and governmental focus on reducing plastic use and increasing sustainability investment continues to create cost and compliance considerations for the industry' - a demand-side and capital-allocation risk to the whole plastics category the Company operates in.
risks.risk: Structural pressure to reduce plastic use / sustainability transition cost

risks.note: MD&A states 'Intense competition in a fragmented market continues to restrict pricing power for smaller participants', which is directly relevant to a company of this scale operating in a single reportable segment.
risks.risk: Intense competition in a fragmented market limiting pricing power

risks.note: 'Trade uncertainties, protectionist policies in key export markets and currency volatility pose ongoing risks to international growth ambitions'; Risks and Concerns adds that global trade uncertainties and supply-chain considerations 'continue to add financial and operational risk for manufacturers'. The Company recorded both foreign exchange earnings and larger foreign exchange outgo during the year, so it carries currency exposure on both sides.
risks.risk: Trade uncertainty, protectionism in export markets and currency volatility

risks.note: The Company 'operates in a single reportable business segment, namely the manufacture of plastic sheets and granules (HIPS, ABS, PET, PP and HDPE)', so there is no segment diversification to absorb a shock to plastics demand, regulation or feedstock costs.

MD&A notes 'Infrastructure gaps and shortages of skilled labour in certain regions continue to constrain scaling and technology adoption for smaller players' - a stated constraint on capacity expansion and technology absorption.
risks.risk: Infrastructure gaps and skilled-labour shortages constraining scaling
